buildSteps.title: Prove cheap access to orbit
buildSteps.detail: Nothing at Dyson scale can be lifted from Earth by chemical rockets, so reusable launch must first collapse the cost per kilogram by orders of magnitude.

buildSteps.title: Mine a low-gravity body
buildSteps.detail: An asteroid or small moon is excavated and its material launched into space by electromagnetic mass drivers rather than rockets.

buildSteps.title: Build factories in orbit
buildSteps.detail: Solar furnaces and 3D printers convert that material into panels, trusses and structural beams, so the collector mass never touches Earth.

buildSteps.title: Deploy the first collectors
buildSteps.detail: Early units are solar power satellites in low or geostationary orbits, beaming power to a rectenna on the ground — the same physics as a Dyson swarm, at tiny scale.

buildSteps.title: Automate replication
buildSteps.detail: Factories are designed so that each generation of machinery builds the next, giving exponential growth in manufacturing capacity.

buildSteps.title: Grow the swarm
buildSteps.detail: Collectors are added in progressively wider orbits until they form a loose shell around the star, each unit independently tracked and steered.

buildSteps.title: Capture and route the power
buildSteps.detail: Energy is beamed to consumers or used in orbit; a partial swarm output already dwarfs all planetary demand.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop on heat and materials
buildSteps.detail: Waste heat must be radiated away, and the swarm's total mass is capped by what can be disassembled from nearby bodies.

prerequisites.tech: Very low-cost launch and in-space transport
prerequisites.why: reusability has cut costs sharply, but the mass needed for even a partial swarm is millions of times beyond current traffic.
no asteroid or lunar mining at industrial scale exists yet; it is the only source of material large enough.
the workforce cannot be supplied from Earth, so machines must build and repair machines.
microwave and laser power transmission has been demonstrated in small experiments but not at grid scale.
billions of independent objects in overlapping orbits risk cascading collisions that would destroy the structure.

pathway.milestone: reusable launch, in-orbit assembly and small solar-power-satellite experiments
pathway.unlocks: routine access to orbit and the beginnings of an off-world manufacturing chain.

pathway.milestone: lunar and asteroid mining feeding orbital factories
pathway.unlocks: structural mass that never has to be launched from Earth.

pathway.milestone: orbital solar farms beaming power to planetary grids
pathway.unlocks: a proven, profitable collector economy — the seed of a swarm.
a partial Dyson swarm capturing a measurable share of a star's output.
energy on the scale of a Kardashev Type II civilisation, with interstellar engineering and travel becoming feasible.
